result.summary: This WIP/RFC PR raises Bitcoin Core's minimum required C++ standard to C++23, bumping minimum GCC to 13 and Clang to 19. It removes several C++20-era workarounds (a hand-written Expected type in favor of std::expected, the ALWAYS_FALSE shim, custom byteswap code) and mechanically replaces std::string::find(...)!=npos patterns with std::string::contains across many files. It also adds a release note and adjusts CI flags to build with an even newer standard (-std=c++26) to catch deprecated code early.
result.problem: Maintainers who write C++ in this codebase currently must avoid C++23-only features and keep workarounds for older compilers, even though some subtrees (e.g. libmultiprocess) already rely on C++23 lambda attributes. The author states the workarounds keep accumulating and wants to unlock newer language and library features once the project decides it's safe to require them.

open_concerns: Author explicitly states 'I don't know when it is fine to switch' -- the core question of whether/when to require C++23 is unresolved.

result.card: This wip/nomerge/rfc PR by a Bitcoin Core maintainer proposes requiring a C++23 compiler (GCC 13+, Clang 19+), removing accumulated C++20 workarounds such as a custom Expected type and ALWAYS_FALSE shim in favor of std::expected, and mechanically replacing find()!=npos idioms with contains() across dozens of files. The stated motivation is that workarounds for pre-C++23 keep accumulating and some subtrees already rely on C++23 features, but the author admits 'I don't know when it is fine to switch,' making this squarely a decision-needed RFC rather than a ready-to-merge change. Review state is Stale: CI is failing, the PR needs rebase, and the author has been silent for over three weeks after several force-pushes. The only substantive feedback is a bare concept ACK from l0rinc and an observational comment from hebasto about an IWYU side effect; no objections have been raised. Its main leverage claim, unlocking unspecified 'new stuff' referenced in a linked issue comment, is not corroborated by other reviewers.
